answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral, but correlated equivocation is aggregated across the detected set: if k identities sign conflicting histories, the penalty grows as O(k^2), so coordination cannot be cheaply partitioned among aliases. Upon detection, controlling the sybil swarm incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation preserves honest stake. A glacier, delta, or vertex in the evidence graph cannot evade shared attribution.
